Reviewer: an isolated contract reviewer at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, read-only on GitHub (REST reads only; nothing written, pushed, labelled or commented), fed the card body and comments, the PR body, the diff against the merge-base, the head's check-runs, contract-review.md and review-checklist.md. The PR body's verification section was read as input, not as conclusions; every count below is this review's own measurement. No environment variable value is printed anywhere in this record, and no advisory, finding or mechanism is named: the diff is rule text and a code comment about the relay's advisory rows.

### ① Derived judgments

1. File surface. One commit (1d36ecfa, author Claude, PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`, trailers `Claude-Session:` + `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, no model identifier). `git diff --numstat dd4a21f8 1d36ecfa`, the REST file listing and the PR body agree on exactly two paths: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/security-findings.md` +1/−1 (blob 5b7442e0 → 7acd15ca), `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` +3/−2 (c328a12c → 4eb92b0d). Total +4/−3. The claim's file surface for PR A (6587178205) was these two paths with stop-on-breach; nothing else is touched. Correct, and on surface.
2. The security-findings.md bullet says what the code does. On the head, `OPS.advisory_report` has `permission: 'repository-advisories'` and no `grant`; `OPS.advisory_create` the same. `validate.mjs`'s `levelOf` returns `OPS[op].grant ?? PERMISSIONS[OPS[op].permission]`, and `PERMISSIONS['repository-advisories']` is `'write'`, so `tokenPermissionsOf` carries `repository-advisories: write` for a stroke of either row; the self-test battery pins all four writing rows to `permission_repository_advisories=write`. The workflow's mint step reads that output as `permission-repository-advisories`, and its own comment states that a refused mint fails the step with zero writes. So on an installation without the advisory write grant, a report stroke and a create stroke both die at the mint: the new bullet's first clause (both rows mint the same advisory write grant; a repository without it refuses both) is what the code does. The old bullet, which kept `advisory_report` for exactly those repositories, named a fallback the relay cannot run; the card's item 1 premise holds against the head and against origin/main. Correct.
3. The bullet's second clause (a private report has a separate per-account daily cap) is what ops.mjs's header says in the same section: GitHub caps the new private reports an account files per day, every relay report is filed as the one App, and the cap does not reach a created draft. The old bullet's "the whole fleet shares one App" nuance is no longer on the skill line; ops.mjs still carries it, the line sits at 116 bytes of a 120-byte budget, and the rule's reader needs the cap, not the quota's sharing, to choose a row. Correct, with that one nuance moved rather than lost.
4. The fallback stays where it was. Bullet 5 of §3 (both operations refused ⇒ session hand-off, option A) is byte-identical to the merge-base and two lines below the reworded one, so the rule still names exactly one path for a repository without the grant, and it is the one the relay can run. The card offered the maintainer a different fallback as an alternative; none was ruled, so the "what the code does" branch is the right one. Correct.
5. The execute.mjs comment names headings that exist. On the head, ops.mjs's header has `## The four rows that touch a security advisory — no advisory text on a public surface` (line 376) and `## The one row that READS an advisory — advisory_read, sealed to a key the seat alone holds` (line 502); the comment's two quoted names are exact prefixes of those two headings, and the `advisory_read` sub-bullet the comment points "below" is in the same block. `git grep` for "three rows that touch" over the whole head tree returns nothing; over origin/main it returns exactly execute.mjs line 195, the one line this PR changes. Correct.
6. No reader of the old text remains, and no other surface says the old thing. `git grep advisory_report` over `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agents/**` on the head returns only the reworded line; the only other stale phrase the card lists ("THREE consumers") is in fleet-write.yml, which this PR leaves alone by the claim's split and PR #29620 carries. Correct.
7. Ratchets and lints. The file is 56 lines against a ceiling of 56 (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` line 1311 row); the reworded line is 116 bytes without its newline (the body's 117 counts the newline), under the 120-byte budget; the ratchet, its 164-case self-test, the id-lint and the skills token ratchet all exit 0 on the head. The three fleet-write self-tests (execute 259, validate 303, dispatch 315 cases) exit 0 without `node_modules`, so a comment-only edit to execute.mjs breaks none of its own batteries. Correct.
8. Governance. `check-governed-merges.mjs --branch HEAD` and `--pr 29619`: 2 paths, 1 register hit (`.claude/**`), Tier S, 7 changed lines under the 3000 threshold, exit 3 as designed; execute.mjs is not on the register. The PR is a draft with no reviews; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on the head. This record is the Tier S at-tier review of record the guard asks for on the current head; landing follows the seat's queue once every check is green. Correct.
9. PR body against the head. First content line `Part of #29448` with the card number beside zero verbs; the body's only issue number is 29448, so no closing keyword sits beside any card and item 3 is named as "a separate Tier H PR" without a number; the `PR-body guards` check is success. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right (no published package, no spec, no changeset; `skip-changeset` and `Check Changeset` success). The body's 56/56, 42 derived commands, "comment only" for execute.mjs and the fallback-stays-at-bullet-five reading all reproduce here. "Part of" is right: the card closes on the last of the two PRs, which is #29620 by the seat's plan. Human Minimum item 3 is left unchecked with a reason (no formatter ran, `pnpm lint` not run locally); `Lint · ESLint` is success on the head, so the gate it stands for is read from CI. Correct.
10. Nothing new on any surface: no gate, no label, no workflow, no register row, no package, no new rule; §8 of the file (no new gates, no new labels) still holds. The card asked for a reword to what the code does; this PR is that, on one line, plus the one cross-reference fix.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no TypeScript; a skill reference file and a comment in a `scripts/pm` tool. `skip-changeset` is the right declaration and Check Changeset is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none in the PR body; the card's one open alternative (the maintainer ruling a different fallback) was not taken up, and the PR chose the branch the card itself names first. No flag.
- Assignee and requested reviewer `huangyiirene` on the PR: the PR's assignee mirrors the card's by `pr_create`, per AGENTS.md; no second claim, no approval, no review submitted. No flag.
- Both branches off `main` at dd4a21f8, not stacked: PR #29620's merge-base is the same commit and its one path is disjoint from this PR's two. Confirmed.
- Independence: PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, commit author Claude; no off-relay author note is owed. The PR thread carries the seat's `Contract-review-claim:` for this head (6589621568) and no other record.
- Tier S: this record is the at-tier review; the owning seat lands through the queue once every check on the head is green (the Check-runs line below).

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (a seat meeting a security finding reads §3 and must be sent to a row the relay can run):

- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/security-findings.md`: rewording the bullet in place, on one line, keeps the file at its ceiling and keeps §3's shape (preferred rows, read row, the report row's standing, the never-as-self rule, the hand-off, private repositories). The new sentence states the grant the two rows share and what a missing grant does to both, which is the one fact the old bullet got wrong, and leaves the hand-off bullet to say what happens next, so the rule has no second fallback and no contradiction. The per-account cap stays because it is the only thing that still distinguishes a report from a draft for the reader. Holds.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`: naming both ops.mjs headings, verbatim as prefixes, is the right fix: the block below already measures the read row with the four writing rows, so pointing at the write section alone would have left the read row's authority unnamed. Comment only; no battery, no export, no behaviour changes, and the three self-tests exit 0. Holds.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix: none.
